title: 1 Kings 2
paragraphs: ¹ As the time drew near for David to die, he gave these instructions to his son Solomon: ² "I am about to go the way of all the earth. Be strong, and show yourself a man. ³ Keep the charge of the LORD your God, walking in his ways and keeping his statutes, his commandments, his rules, and his testimonies, as written in the law of Moses. Then you will succeed in everything you do and wherever you turn — ⁴ so that the LORD may fulfill his promise to me: 'If your sons take care how they walk before me in faithfulness with all their heart and soul, you shall never lack a man on the throne of Israel.' ⁵ You also know what Joab son of Zeruiah did to me — what he did to the two commanders of Israel's armies, Abner son of Ner and Amasa son of Jether. He killed them both, shedding the blood of war in peacetime, staining his belt and his sandals with the blood of men he murdered.

⁶ Act according to your wisdom, and do not let his gray head go down to the grave in peace. ⁷ But deal loyally with the sons of Barzillai the Gileadite and let them be among those who eat at your table, because they came to help me when I was fleeing from your brother Absalom. ⁸ You also have with you Shimei son of Gera, the Benjaminite from Bahurim. He cursed me with a bitter curse the day I went to Mahanaim, but then he came down to meet me at the Jordan and I swore to him by the LORD that I would not kill him with the sword. ⁹ Do not let him go unpunished. You are a wise man and you know what to do — bring his gray head down to the grave with blood." ¹⁰ Then David rested with his ancestors and was buried in the City of David.

¹¹ David had reigned over Israel for forty years — seven years in Hebron and thirty-three years in Jerusalem. ¹² Solomon then sat on the throne of his father David, and his rule was firmly established. ¹³ Adonijah son of Haggith came to Bathsheba, the mother of Solomon. "Do you come in peace?" she asked. "Yes, in peace," he said. ¹⁴ "I have something to say to you." "Go ahead," she said. ¹⁵ He said, "You know that the kingdom was mine, and all Israel expected me to be king. But things turned around, and the kingdom went to my brother instead — because it was the LORD's doing.

¹⁶ Now I have one request to make of you — don't refuse me." "What is it?" she asked. ¹⁷ He said, "Please speak to King Solomon — he won't refuse you — and ask him to give me Abishag the Shunammite as my wife." ¹⁸ "Very well," Bathsheba said, "I will speak to the king for you." ¹⁹ So Bathsheba went to King Solomon to speak on Adonijah's behalf. The king rose to meet her and bowed to her. Then he sat back down on his throne and had a throne set for the king's mother, and she sat at his right hand. ²⁰ "I have one small request to make of you," she said. "Don't refuse me." "Ask, my mother," the king replied, "for I will not refuse you."

²¹ She said, "Let Abishag the Shunammite be given to your brother Adonijah as his wife." ²² King Solomon answered his mother, "Why do you ask Abishag the Shunammite for Adonijah? You might as well ask for the kingdom for him — he is my older brother, and Abiathar the priest and Joab son of Zeruiah are on his side." ²³ Then King Solomon swore by the LORD: "May God deal with me severely if Adonijah does not pay with his life for this request. ²⁴ Now, as the LORD lives — who has established me and placed me on the throne of my father David and built a dynasty for me just as he promised — Adonijah will be put to death today." ²⁵ King Solomon gave the order to Benaiah son of Jehoiada, who struck Adonijah down, and he died.

²⁶ To Abiathar the priest the king said, "Go to your estate in Anathoth. You deserve to die, but I will not put you to death now, because you carried the ark of the Lord GOD before my father David, and you shared in all the hardships my father endured." ²⁷ So Solomon dismissed Abiathar from serving as priest to the LORD, fulfilling the word the LORD had spoken at Shiloh concerning the house of Eli. ²⁸ When Joab heard this — Joab had sided with Adonijah, though not with Absalom — he fled to the tent of the LORD and grabbed hold of the horns of the altar. ²⁹ King Solomon was told that Joab had fled to the tent of the LORD and was beside the altar. So Solomon sent Benaiah son of Jehoiada with orders to strike him down. ³⁰ Benaiah came to the tent of the LORD and said to Joab, "The king says to come out." But Joab replied, "No — I will die here." Benaiah reported this back to the king.

³¹ The king said to Benaiah, "Do what he says. Strike him down and bury him. Take away from me and from my father's house the guilt of the blood Joab shed without cause. ³² The LORD will repay him for the blood he shed — he killed two men who were more righteous and better than he, cutting them down with the sword when my father David knew nothing of it: Abner son of Ner, commander of Israel's army, and Amasa son of Jether, commander of Judah's army. ³³ Their blood will rest on Joab's head and on his descendants' heads forever. But on David, and on his descendants, his house and his throne, may there be peace from the LORD forever." ³⁴ Benaiah son of Jehoiada went up and struck Joab down and killed him, and he was buried at his own property in the wilderness. ³⁵ The king then appointed Benaiah son of Jehoiada as commander of the army in Joab's place, and put Zadok the priest in place of Abiathar.

³⁶ The king also summoned Shimei and said to him, "Build yourself a house in Jerusalem and live there. Do not go anywhere else. ³⁷ The day you leave and cross the Kidron Valley, you can be certain you will die. Your blood will be on your own head." ³⁸ "What my lord the king says is fair," Shimei replied. "Your servant will do what you say." And Shimei lived in Jerusalem for a long time. ³⁹ But three years later, two of Shimei's servants ran off to Achish son of Maacah, the king of Gath. Shimei was told, "Your servants are in Gath." ⁴⁰ So Shimei saddled his donkey and went to Gath to Achish in search of his servants. He went and brought them back from Gath.

⁴¹ Solomon was told that Shimei had gone from Jerusalem to Gath and returned. ⁴² The king summoned Shimei and said to him, "Did I not make you swear by the LORD and warn you clearly: 'On the day you leave and go anywhere, you can be certain you will die'? And you said to me, 'What you say is fair, and I accept it.' ⁴³ Why then did you not keep the oath you swore to the LORD and the command I gave you?" ⁴⁴ The king also said to Shimei, "You know in your own heart all the wrong you did to my father David. The LORD will now repay you for it. ⁴⁵ But King Solomon will be blessed, and David's throne will remain established before the LORD forever."
⁴⁶ The king gave the order to Benaiah son of Jehoiada, who went out and struck Shimei down. He died. The kingdom was now firmly in Solomon's hands.
